subject: Consequential damages exclusion — mutual vs one-way language (MSA + Order Form redlines)
body:
-----Original Message-----
From: Daniel Price <daniel.price@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kris Nguyen <kris.nguyen@brightlinehealth.com>, legal@brightlinehealth.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — liability carve-outs

Sergio,

Thanks again for the redlines. Our general counsel flagged the consequential damages exclusion as a sticking point. They insist on one-way language (no recovery by Brightline for indirect/consequential damages, but Redwood remains liable for consequential damages caused by Redwood's gross negligence, willful misconduct, and proven data breaches that lead to patient harm).

We tried to propose a middle ground in the attached PDF (OrderForm-Brightline_v3_redline.pdf) that keeps the exclusion one-way but carves out damages for: (a) breach of confidentiality involving PHI, (b) bodily injury/death, (c) gross negligence and willful misconduct, and (d) claims arising from Redwood's indemnity obligations.

Can your legal team confirm whether that compromise is acceptable to Redwood? If not, can you share Redwood's rationale for requiring mutual exclusion on consequential damages?

Best,
Daniel

--
Daniel Price
Head of Finance & Ops
Brightline Health
D: 415-555-0199

>
> Quick ask: can you confirm whether Brightline's position is that Redwood remains fully liable for consequential damages caused by Redwood's negligence (ordinary or gross), or only for gross negligence/willful misconduct and certain PHI events? The distinction changes how we approach caps and mutuality.
>
> I also attached our working MSA redline (MSA-Brightline_redline.docx) and an "Exhibit A" liability matrix to show tradeoffs (who eats what risk).
>
> Proposed next step: 30-min call today 4:00pm PT to resolve points so Finance can move procurement along. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

On Mon, May 4, 2026 at 10:03 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com> wrote:

> From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
> To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
> Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
> Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form — liability carve-outs>
>
> Team — quick read-through notes from legal:
>
> 1) Mutual vs one-way: Redwood prefers a mutual consequential damages exclusion. Our standard position is mutual exclusions for indirect/special/incidental damages to avoid asymmetric exposure that could be negotiated away in future iterations. We will accept one-way only in narrow scenarios where customer carries insurance or there is a different commercial leverage (e.g., large committed spend).
>
> 2) Carve-outs we can accept: breach of confidentiality (PHI/PII), bodily injury/death, Redwood's indemnity obligations, and claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
>
> 3) Definition fight: Brightline's redline uses a broad definition of consequential damages that calls out lost profits, lost business, and punitive damages. We should push to (a) keep the definition narrow — "indirect, special, or consequential" — and (b) expressly exclude punitive damages from caps but keep them out of the consequential-exclusion carve-out except where expressly carved (e.g., bodily injury).
>
> 4) Cap interplay: If Brightline insists on Redwood being liable for certain consequential damages, we need to ensure those damages fall within the overall liability cap (typically the greater of fees paid in prior 12 months or $X). If they want uncapped consequential liability for PHI leading to patient harm, we need to state that expressly.
>
> I've drafted two alternate clauses in the attached MSA redline: (A) Mutual exclusion with standard carve-outs, (B) One-way customer-favored exclusion with explicit uncapped carve-out for PHI causing bodily injury. Please review, especially Markus on indemnity linkage.
>
> Laura Bennett
> Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
> Redwood Inference
> l.bennett@redwoodinference.com | 650-555-0147
>

On Mon, May 4, 2026 at 11:20 AM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com> wrote:

> From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>

> Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
> Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form — liability carve-outs>
>
> Laura — agreed on the carve-outs list. A couple of drafting nits from my side: 
>
> - Indemnity linkage: if indemnity claims (e.g., third-party IP claims) are carved out of the consequential exclusion, make sure the indemnity paragraph requires Redwood to defend and indemnify "to the extent resulting in damages otherwise excluded as consequential". Also make sure the remedy/cost recoverability language doesn't inadvertently recreate consequential exposure (e.g., attorneys' fees that morph into lost business claims).
>
> - Punitive damages: add clearer language that punitive damages are not recoverable unless awarded by a court in a final judgment relating to willful misconduct or fraud. Keeps recoverability narrow.
>
> - Cap math: propose cap equal to the greater of (i) fees paid by Brightline in prior 12 months, or (ii) $1M for this deal class. If Brightline pushes for higher, we can trade for narrower indemnity scope.
>
> I'll mark up the indemnity cross‑reference in the MSA redline and push the cap language into Exhibit A.
>
> Markus Klein
> General Counsel
> Redwood Inference
> markus.klein@redwoodinference.com | 415-555-0101
>

On Tue, May 5, 2026 at 09:41 AM Kris Nguyen <kris.nguyen@brightlinehealth.com> wrote:

> Cc: Daniel Price <daniel.price@brightlinehealth.com>, legal@brightlinehealth.com
> Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:41:00 -07:00
> Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form — liability carve-outs>
>
> Thanks all — quick answers from Brightline legal below and inline in the attachment: 
>
> - Brightline will not accept a mutual consequential damages exclusion that absolves Redwood from liability for data breaches that lead to patient harm. We need an explicit uncapped carve-out for PHI breaches that cause bodily injury or regulatory fines.
>
> - On punitive damages: we will accept the court-ordered limitation language, but we reserve the right to seek exemplary damages where permitted by law for gross negligence or willful misconduct.
>
> - Cap ask: Brightline can accept a 12-month fees cap only if the PHI/PII carve-out is uncapped. Otherwise we want a higher base cap ($5M).
>
> We are open to agreeing mutual exclusion language if Redwood accepts the uncapped PHI carve-out and the indemnity linkage described above. See attached OrderForm-Brightline_v3_redline.pdf for our edits and a proposed execution-ready Order Form.
>
> Can we lock language on the two options by COB tomorrow? We have internal procurement timelines.
>
> Kris Nguyen
> Director, Procurement
> Brightline Health
> kris.nguyen@brightlinehealth.com | 212-555-0168
>
>

> Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — liability carve-outs>
>
> Hi Daniel / Kris — thanks for the clarity and for marking up the Order Form. We want to propose a final two-option pathway so procurement can execute depending on risk appetite: 
>
> Option 1 (Standard): Mutual consequential damages exclusion with the following carve-outs: (i) breach of confidentiality involving PHI/PII that leads to bodily injury, (ii) Redwood's gross negligence/willful misconduct, (iii) liability arising from Redwood's indemnity obligations. Consequential damages for other commercial loss (lost profits / lost business) remain excluded. Cap = greater of prior 12 months fees or $1M.
>
> Option 2 (Customer-favored): One-way exclusion in Brightline's favor with explicit uncapped carve-out for PHI breaches causing bodily injury and uncapped indemnity for IP claims tied to patient harm. Cap = $5M.
>
> If Brightline confirms preference for Option 2, we will accept that commercially but require execution of the attached Order Form and confirmation of insurance limits (cyber liability >= $5M). If Brightline prefers Option 1, we need a signature and routing update to the procurement PO flow.
>
> Please reply with which option you want and we will circulate a final MSA + Order Form for signature.
>
> Regards,
>Vanessa Ortiz
>Sr. Solutions Counsel
>Redwood Inference
